paragraphs: Friend, here is what I love about this prayer. The man doesn't clean himself up before he talks to God. He is worn out, lonely and hurting, and he pours all of it out before the LORD (Psalm 102:1). If you've ever thought you had to be fine before you could pray, this psalm says come as you are.

Now watch what happens at the little word "But." His days fade like shadows, and he says the LORD "sit[s] enthroned forever" (Psalm 102:12). He doesn't pretend the pain isn't real. He just stops staring at it long enough to look up. And the LORD "will not despise their prayer" (Psalm 102:17), so a prayer from a tired baker is never too small for Him.

Here's the part that gets me, friend. The earth and the heavens will wear out like a garment, but the man tells God, "You remain the same, and Your years will never end" (Psalm 102:26-27). Everything you lean on is fading, and the LORD is not. So the next time your days feel like smoke, do what this man did: pour it out, look up, and lean on the One who stays.
